lead: Keerthi K P (born 22 April 2006) is an Indian computer science student pursuing a Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering at R.M.D. Engineering College, Chennai. She specializes in Cybersecurity and is pursuing an honors track in Artificial Intelligence. Her interests include cybersecurity, open-source intelligence (OSINT), digital forensics, software development and artificial intelligence. She has participated in programming competitions, hackathons and cybersecurity events.

sections.title: Early life and education
paragraphs: Keerthi was born on 22 April 2006 in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. She began her schooling at Ebenezer Marcus Matriculation School, where she studied from kindergarten, before attending Velammal Vidyalaya, Melayanambakkam, through Class XII.

Her early interest in technology developed through experimenting with computer settings and helping others troubleshoot technical problems. She was introduced to programming through turtle graphics during middle school, where she experimented with controlling on-screen movement through basic commands.

She later learned Microsoft Excel and studied Python as a major subject in higher secondary school. She completed Class XII in the Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics stream with Computer Science, graduating in May 2023 with 87%.

In August 2023, she enrolled at R.M.D. Engineering College to pursue a Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering, specializing in Cybersecurity with honors in Artificial Intelligence.

images.caption: Velammal Vidyalaya, where Keerthi studied through Class XII.

subsections.title: Infosys Springboard
paragraphs: Between December 2024 and February 2025, Keerthi worked as a Python intern at Infosys Springboard, contributing to the Unified Family Finance Tracker.

The project was a full-stack budgeting platform supporting multiple user profiles and expense categories. She contributed to the expense management module and served as Scrum Master and Product Manager, coordinating project delivery, team activities and module integration.

subsections.title: Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing
paragraphs: From June to July 2026, Keerthi worked with the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing on an Android APK malware analysis tool.

Her contribution focused on frontend development. She redesigned the interface to improve usability and accessibility for non-technical users and simplified the presentation of malware analysis results.

items.name: ViewLing
items.description: An individual project to visualize exported WhatsApp conversations and present chat data in a more accessible visual form. The project is being developed for personal family use.

items.name: PhishMate / PhishMateBERT
items.description: A phishing-detection browser extension initiated as PhishMate during FOSS Hack 2025 and later developed into PhishMateBERT. The later iteration uses a DeBERTa-based classification approach.

image.caption: PhishMate and its subsequent iteration, PhishMateBERT.

items.name: ParamStock
items.description: An individual stock-monitoring and notification project. It uses Yahoo Finance data and Twilio to send stock alerts through WhatsApp, with Flask as the application backend.

image.alt: ParamStock dashboard or WhatsApp alert screenshot
image.caption: ParamStock stock-monitoring and WhatsApp alert interface.

items.name: TimeCapsule
items.description: A decentralized internet archival project designed to preserve web content with verifiable integrity, using SHA-256 hashing, IPFS and OpenTimestamps. The project received second runner-up recognition at Defy'26.

items.name: Dust Buster
items.description: A hardware prototype developed by a four-member team for the Science Day Project Expo at R.M.D. Engineering College. It uses an Arduino Uno and an ultrasonic distance sensor to detect dust or particles inside a chalk box and trigger an alert. The project was a finalist at the expo and was framed around UN Sustainable Development Goal 9.

image.caption: Dust Buster hardware prototype. Project documentation supplied by Keerthi.

items.name: YapFormer
items.description: A team project involving a transformer-based language model built from scratch. Keerthi contributed to the console interface and terminal-based user experience; she did not develop the model architecture.

sections.title: Leadership and event organization
paragraphs: Keerthi served as lead organizer of ClawCTF, a cybersecurity competition held as part of Rendezvous 2k26, the Computer Science and Engineering symposium at R.M.D. Engineering College.
Her responsibilities included event management and the creation of OSINT challenges. The event covered multiple cybersecurity domains and received more than 60 registrations.
